info.title: Agentiik API
info.summary: The identity and access routes of /api/v1: signing in, the authentication policy, the caller, users, groups, service accounts, namespaces and their quotas, grants and API tokens.
info.description: One description of the access routes of /api/v1 for the three clients that speak them, agk, the console and the Terraform provider, so that none of them learns the API from another's code. It describes the routes of v0.3.0 and no other yet; tools/check.py holds its routes to the table at https://agentiik.github.io/docs#api and names every route of the table this document does not describe. Every record the API shares with the rest of the contract, a user, a grant, a token, a namespace, the policy, is a reference into wire.schema.json beside it rather than a copy, so that the two cannot drift; a consumer resolves the references relative to this document. What is defined here is what only a route carries: a request body, a list, a token shown once, Web Authentication's own JSON forms. Every body is JSON of at most 64 KiB, closed to fields the route does not read, save Web Authentication's own objects, which are the browser's to extend. Every refusal is {"error"}, and a namespace or a workflow the caller cannot see is refused as one that does not exist, so that no name can be learnt by asking.

externalDocs.description: The documentation, which decides what the API does: this document follows it.

servers.description: An installation, at the address people and clients reach it by.

host.description: The host of AGK_PUBLIC_URL, or of AGK_PROXY_URL behind a reverse proxy, with its port where it is not 443. It is also the Relying Party Identifier every passkey is bound to.

tags.name: sign-in
tags.description: Proving who one is: the passkey ceremony, the password fallback, the pages the API serves on the Relying Party's origin, and agk login's exchange.

tags.name: policy
tags.description: The authentication policy, set once for the installation and tightened, never loosened, by a namespace.

tags.name: me
tags.description: The caller: who it is, what it may do, and its own credentials.

tags.name: tokens
tags.description: API tokens, minted, listed and revoked one by one, never shown twice.

tags.name: users
tags.description: Local accounts, and the links and codes that enrol their passkeys.

tags.name: groups
tags.description: Named sets of users, which grants target so that membership changes touch no grant.

tags.name: service-accounts
tags.description: Non-human principals of a namespace, holding API tokens only.

tags.name: namespaces
tags.description: Namespaces and their quotas, an administrator's to create and bound.

tags.name: grants
tags.description: Sharing: grants and denies at namespace and workflow scope.

post.description: Answers the options a browser hands navigator.credentials: a fresh challenge, the Relying Party Identifier, which is the host of AGK_PUBLIC_URL or of AGK_PROXY_URL behind a proxy, and the user verification the policy imposes. An assertion asks for whichever passkey the authenticator holds for this Relying Party, so no login is sent before the ceremony and none can be probed for. A registration names the user being enrolled and excludes the passkeys they already hold; it needs a session, an enrolment-only one included, or the code of an enrolment link or a recovery code. The challenge is single use, consumed by the verification that follows. An installation addressed by an IP address answers no options, since a browser runs no ceremony there.

requestBody.description: The ceremony to start, and the enrolment code where a registration has no session behind it.

enrolment link.summary: a registration from an enrolment link

another passkey.summary: a signed-in user adding a passkey

200.description: The options, to hand to PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON() or parseRequestOptionsFromJSON() as they are.

400.description: The body is refused, or carries a code beside an assertion.

401.description: A registration with neither a session nor a code, or with a code that opens nothing: used, lapsed or revoked.

409.description: The installation is addressed by an IP address, which a browser refuses as a Relying Party Identifier.

post.description: Verifies the browser's answer to the options, an attestation for a registration and an assertion for a sign-in, with the Go standard library alone and no attestation asked for or checked. It records the Backup Eligibility and Backup State flags, refuses a synced passkey where device_bound_only is set, and requires user verification where the policy does. A registration records the passkey, audited as credential.enrol, and consumes the enrolment code where one opened the ceremony, audited as enrolment.use; where the policy requires passkeys, a user reaching min_passkeys has their password hash deleted rather than disabled. An assertion opens a full session, set in the cookie of the answer, audited as signin.succeed or signin.fail, and, for a sign-in agk login started, answers the loopback address to send the browser to, carrying a one-time code for POST /api/v1/auth/exchange.

requestBody.description: The browser's answer, with the label of a new passkey or what agk login opened the page with.

200.description: The ceremony verified: the passkey recorded, or the account signed in.

Set-Cookie.description: The session an assertion opened. Absent after a registration, which opens none.

400.description: The body is refused, or pairs a label with an assertion or terminal with a registration.

401.description: An attestation or an assertion that does not verify: a challenge not issued or already used, an origin or a Relying Party that is not this one, an unknown credential, a signature that does not check, user verification missing where it is required, or an account that opens no session. One sentence for every one of them, so that a failure teaches nothing about which part was wrong.

403.description: A synced passkey, at registration or at sign-in, where device_bound_only applies to the account; the error names the setting.

get.description: The page the API serves on the Relying Party's origin to sign in: the passkey ceremony, and the password fallback where the policy allows it, nothing more. It is embedded in agentiik-api and loads nothing from anywhere else, because a passkey ceremony runs only on a page of the Relying Party's origin and the console comes in its own releases. agk login opens it with the loopback address it listens on and the SHA-256 of a one-time verifier, which the page hands on with the sign-in, so that the browser ends on the loopback address with a one-time code.

page.value:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>Sign in to Agentiik</title></head>
<body>...</body>
</html>

400.description: One of redirect_uri and code_challenge without the other, or a value outside its grammar: a page that would hand a code to a host other than the loopback is never served.

get.description: The page that enrols a passkey from an enrolment link or a recovery code, on the Relying Party's origin. A link carries its code after #, which a browser never sends, so the code reaches no access log: the page reads it from its own address and sends it in the body of POST /api/v1/auth/passkey/options. A recovery code is typed into the page instead.

post.summary: Trade agk login's code for an API token
post.description: The last step of agk login: the one-time code the sign-in page sent the browser back to the loopback address with, and the verifier whose SHA-256 opened the page, answered with an API token for the user who signed in. It is PKCE's exchange (RFC 7636): a code seen on the way, in the browser's history or by another process on the machine, opens nothing without the verifier, which never left agk. The code is single use and good for a minute. The token is minted as POST /api/v1/auth/tokens mints one, expiring after 90 days, and audited as api_token.create.

401.description: A code that opens nothing: used already, older than a minute, never issued, or presented with a verifier whose SHA-256 is not the challenge it was issued against. One sentence for all of them.

get.description: The installation's authentication policy, every setting written out, a default included, so that nobody needs to know the defaults to know what applies. Any authenticated principal may read it. A namespace's tightening is read at GET /api/v1/{ns}/auth/policy.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

put.description: Replaces the installation's policy, as agk auth policy does with settings given: a setting the body leaves out returns to its default, so that the body is the whole of the policy. Administrator only, and audited as policy.change. Forbidding passwords deletes every stored password hash and suspends the accounts that hold no passkey yet, rather than leaving them reachable by a password the policy says no longer exists. A namespace that asked for more keeps it, since what applies is the stricter of the two, setting by setting.

requestBody.description: The whole policy. An empty object returns every setting to its default.

200.description: The policy as it now stands, every setting present.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

409.description: The installation is addressed by an IP address, where a browser runs no passkey ceremony, and the policy requires a passkey or forbids passwords; the error names the setting.

get.summary: Read a namespace's tightening of the policy
get.description: The namespace's own settings and only those, a setting it leaves out inheriting the installation's value, so that what PUT wrote reads back as it was written. What applies to someone holding a grant in the namespace is the stricter of this and the installation's policy, setting by setting. Readable by an administrator and by every principal holding a grant in the namespace, since the policy applies to them.

200.description: The namespace's own settings; an empty object where it tightens nothing.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such namespace, or one the caller holds nothing in and does not administer.

put.summary: Set a namespace's tightening of the policy
put.description: Replaces the namespace's own settings, as agk auth policy --namespace does; an empty object removes them all, and the namespace inherits every setting. Administrator only, and audited as policy.change. A setting looser than the installation's is refused naming it: password allowed where the installation forbids passwords, passkey optional where it requires one, user_verification preferred where it requires it, device_bound_only false where it is true, or a min_passkeys below the installation's. A namespace may tighten, never loosen.

requestBody.description: The namespace's settings, each one tightening the installation's.

device-bound.summary: device-bound passkeys for everyone holding a grant here

200.description: The namespace's own settings as they now stand.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, which is answered before the namespace is looked up and so says nothing of whether it exists; or it holds an enrolment-only session.

409.description: A setting looser than the installation's; the error names it.

post.description: Signs in with a login and a password where the policy allows passwords, and a TOTP code where the account holds a generator. Refused outright when passwords are forbidden, with a 403 naming the setting and before any password is compared, not failed as a wrong password: a client then knows to stop offering the form. The password is checked against its Argon2id hash. Where the policy requires a passkey the account does not hold, the session is enrolment-only, reaching the registration ceremony and nothing else. Audited as signin.succeed or signin.fail. For a sign-in agk login started, the answer carries the loopback address to send the browser to, as a passkey sign-in's does, which is how agk login signs in on an installation addressed by an IP address.

200.description: Signed in; the session is the cookie set beside this answer.

401.description: A login, a password or a TOTP code that does not match, or an account that opens no session. One sentence for all of them, so that no login can be learnt by asking.

403.description: Passwords are forbidden by the policy that applies to the account; the error names the setting password.

get.description: The caller's credentials: its passkeys, with the kind, flags, label and last use of each, the password where one is still stored, and a TOTP generator where one is enrolled. Never a public key, a hash or a shared secret. A service account holds none.

moving off passwords.summary: a password and a first passkey

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

delete.summary: Remove one of the caller's credentials
delete.description: Removes one of the caller's credentials, audited as credential.remove. A removal that would leave the account below the policy's min_passkeys is refused: a passkey where fewer would remain, and the password where the account holds fewer passkeys than that, so that losing a device is an inconvenience rather than an incident.

400.description: No id, or one outside its grammar.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

404.description: The caller holds no credential by that id.

409.description: The removal would leave the account below min_passkeys; the error names the setting.

post.description: A new enrolment link for a user who holds no credential yet: single use, good for an hour, and revoking any link issued before it, so that a link that lapsed unused locks nobody out. Administrator only, and the bootstrap token's for the first administrator until one has enrolled. Audited as enrolment.issue. The link opens the enrolment page with its code after #, which a browser never sends, so the code reaches no access log; it is shown once and stored hashed.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

409.description: The user already holds a credential; a lost one is replaced with a recovery code.

post.description: A recovery code for a user who has lost their passkeys: single use, good for an hour, authorising the enrolment of a new passkey and nothing else. Administrator only, and audited as enrolment.issue with both identities, the administrator who issued it and the account it is for. The administrator hands it over; it is never sent by mail, which would put the account back behind a mailbox and forfeit the passkey's resistance to phishing.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

post.description: Mints an API token for the caller, or for a service account of a namespace the caller owns: 256 bits of entropy, stored hashed, its value shown in this answer and never again. It expires after 90 days unless the request asks for another expiry, and after a year at most, so that a token forgotten in a script stops on its own and none is a credential for good. An optional scope narrows it and can only narrow: on every request its rights are its principal's intersected with the scope. Audited as api_token.create. An enrolment-only session cannot mint one, and neither can a token narrowed by a scope, whose narrowing a token it minted would otherwise escape.

requestBody.description: What to mint; an empty object mints the caller a token for 90 days with its full rights.

service account.summary: a narrowed token for a service account
a narrowed token for a service account

403.description: An enrolment-only session, or a token narrowed by a scope.

422.description: An expiry already passed or more than a year away, or a principal that is neither the caller nor a service account of a namespace it owns.

get.description: The caller's tokens and those of the service accounts of namespaces it owns, each with its expiry, last use, device label and scope, never a value, so that a token nobody uses can be seen and revoked.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

delete.description: Revokes one token, from its next request: the caller's own, the one making this request included, or one of a service account of a namespace the caller owns. Audited as api_token.revoke.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

404.description: No token by that identifier the caller may revoke.

get.description: The caller's identity, group memberships, effective permissions per namespace, and notifications, such as an administrator having widened their own access in a namespace the caller owns. What agk whoami prints, and what the console reads to hide what the caller does not hold rather than disable it.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

post.description: Creates a shared namespace with an owner and, optionally, quotas. Administrator only, and audited as namespace.create. Its name is refused where a login holds it, since logins and namespace names share one name space: a user's personal namespace is named after their login, and a namespace created first would take it from them. The reserved words the API's first path segment routes on are refused by the grammar. The namespace's built-in identity, NS/agentiik, is created with it and holds no grant until an owner gives it one.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

409.description: The name is held by a namespace or a login.

422.description: An owner that names no user or group, or a quota naming a runner pool that does not exist.

get.description: The namespaces the caller holds a grant in, directly or through a group, and every one for an administrator. A namespace the caller holds nothing in is absent here as it is from every answer.

namespaces.summary: a personal and a shared one

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

get.description: The namespace's quotas, allowed_runner_pools among them, as an administrator last set them. A quota absent sets no bound of the namespace's own. Readable by an administrator and by every principal holding a grant in the namespace.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such namespace, or one the caller holds nothing in and does not administer.

put.description: Replaces the namespace's quotas: a quota the body leaves out sets no bound any more, so that the body is the whole of what applies and an apply reads back what it wrote. Administrator only, and audited as namespace.update. allowed_runner_pools names at least one pool, since a pool's own empty list of namespaces means every one and the same spelling here would be read as its opposite.

requestBody.description: The whole of the namespace's quotas.

200.description: The quotas as they now stand.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, which is answered before the namespace is looked up; or it holds an enrolment-only session.

422.description: A runner pool that does not exist.

get.description: Every user of the installation, with whether each is an administrator and whether it is suspended, and never a credential. Administrator only.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

post.description: Creates a user from a login, a display name and admin where it is an administrator, answered with an enrolment link shown once, single use and good for an hour. Administrator only, save the first administrator, whom the bootstrap token creates as agk user create LOGIN --admin does. Asked again for a user who has not enrolled yet, with the same login, display name and admin, it answers a fresh link and revokes the one before, so that a link that lapsed unused locks nobody out; the bootstrap token relies on this until the first administrator has enrolled, and ends then. The login is refused where a namespace or another user holds it, and operator and the reserved words are refused by its grammar. Audited as user.create, and the link as enrolment.issue.

200.description: The same user asked for again before enrolling: a fresh link, the one before revoked.

201.description: The user created, and the link.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, and is not the bootstrap token before the first administrator has enrolled; or it holds an enrolment-only session.

409.description: The login is held by a namespace, by a user who has enrolled, or by one created with another display name or admin.

get.description: Every group, with its members. Administrator only.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

post.description: Creates a group, empty or with its first members. Administrator only. A group's members are logins and never a group, because a group inside a group would turn effective permissions into a graph walk. Grants target groups so that membership changes without touching a grant.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

409.description: A group already holds the name.

422.description: A member that is no user.

put.summary: Add a member to a group
put.description: Adds one user to the group, touching no grant: every grant written against the group reaches them from their next request. Adding someone already a member changes nothing and answers the same. Administrator only. No body.

200.description: The group as it now stands.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

404.description: No such group, or no such user.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a group
delete.description: Removes one user from the group, touching no grant: what the group's grants gave them ends from their next request. Removing someone who is not a member changes nothing and answers the same. Administrator only.

200.description: The group as it now stands.

403.description: The caller is not an administrator, or holds an enrolment-only session.

get.description: The service accounts of the namespaces the caller owns, the built-in NS/agentiik of each among them. Their tokens are listed at GET /api/v1/auth/tokens.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

post.description: Creates a service account in a namespace the caller owns, written NS/NAME wherever a principal is written: a non-human principal that holds API tokens, minted at POST /api/v1/auth/tokens, and cannot sign in to a client. The authentication policy does not apply to it, and it holds no grant until one is written for it.

400.description: The body is refused, or names the account agentiik, the built-in identity's name in every namespace.

403.description: An enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else.

409.description: The namespace already has a service account of that name.

422.description: A namespace the caller does not own, answered as one that does not exist.

delete.description: Removes a service account of a namespace the caller owns, and revokes its tokens with it. The built-in NS/agentiik is refused: the namespace's scheduled, webhook and event runs are attributed to it, and removing it would leave them attributed to nobody.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such service account, or one of a namespace the caller does not own.

get.description: The grants and denies written on the namespace, each inherited by every workflow in it. Requires grant:manage at namespace scope, since the list names everyone who holds access.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such namespace, or one where the caller does not hold grant:manage: the same answer.

post.description: Writes a grant or a deny on the namespace: a principal as it is written, a role or a deny naming one permission, and an optional expiry that ends it without anyone remembering to revoke it. Requires grant:manage at namespace scope, and is audited as grant.create. An administrator granting themselves access notifies every owner of the namespace in their GET /api/v1/me: that is how an administrator reads another namespace's payloads, since they hold no run:read_data of their own.

400.description: The body is refused, or carries both a role and a deny, or neither.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such namespace, or one where the caller does not hold grant:manage.

422.description: A principal that does not exist, or an expiry already passed.

delete.description: Revokes one grant or deny written on the namespace, from the next request and the next run creation: a trigger armed under it still fires, and the run it creates ends cancelled before any task, naming the grant that lapsed. Requires grant:manage at namespace scope, and is audited as grant.delete.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such grant on this namespace, no such namespace, or one where the caller does not hold grant:manage.

get.summary: List the grants that apply to a workflow
get.description: The grants and denies that apply to the workflow, with the scope of each: those written on it, and those of its namespace, which it inherits. What agk grants reads. Requires grant:manage on the workflow.

200.description: The grants and denies that apply.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such workflow, or one where the caller does not hold grant:manage: the same answer.

post.description: Writes a grant or a deny on the workflow, as agk share does: a principal, a role or a deny naming one permission, and an optional expiry. A workflow-scope grant only adds to what the namespace gives, and only a deny subtracts, winning over any allow at any scope. Requires grant:manage on the workflow, and is audited as grant.create.

operator.summary: a group runs the workflow until January

400.description: The body is refused, or carries both a role and a deny, or neither.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such workflow, or one where the caller does not hold grant:manage.

422.description: A principal that does not exist, or an expiry already passed.

delete.description: Revokes one grant or deny written on the workflow, from the next request and the next run creation. An open log stream asks again every 30 s for its credential and run:read, and ends once either is gone. A grant written on the namespace is revoked at the namespace's route and answers 404 here. Requires grant:manage on the workflow, and is audited as grant.delete.

403.description: Only for an enrolment-only session, which enrols passkeys and nothing else. Every other refusal here is a 404.

404.description: No such grant written on this workflow, no such workflow, or one where the caller does not hold grant:manage.

bearer.description: An API token in the Authorization header, as agk, the mobile applications, the Terraform provider and every script present one: minted at POST /api/v1/auth/tokens or by agk login's exchange, stored hashed, shown once, expiring after 90 days unless asked otherwise and after a year at most. Until the first administrator has enrolled a passkey, the bootstrap token, AGENTIIK_OPERATOR_TOKEN, is presented the same way; it is refused from then on.

session.name: __Host-agentiik_session
session.description: The browser's session: an opaque identifier in a cookie set HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax by the answer that opened it, revocable server-side and ending after a time idle. SameSite=Lax keeps a page of another site from carrying it on a POST, a PUT or a DELETE. The __Host- prefix makes a browser refuse the cookie unless it is Secure, set for the whole origin and bound to no Domain, so no other host under the same domain can set it. The session records the credential that opened it, so an enrolment-only session is known to the server rather than by convention, and reaches the registration ceremony and nothing else.

error.title: Error
error.description: A refusal: one sentence saying what was refused, and, where a setting of the authentication policy is the reason, that setting's name. It says nothing a caller could not already know, which is why a namespace or a workflow the caller cannot see is refused with the same sentence as one that does not exist. The same shape as every refusal the API already answers.
What was refused, in one sentence meant for the person reading it. A client shows it and matches nothing against it: the status is what a program branches on.
examples: no such thing, or not yours
you do not hold what this needs
removing this passkey would leave fewer than min_passkeys

setting.description: The setting of the authentication policy the refusal is about, spelled as the policy spells it: a setting a namespace's policy would loosen, one an installation addressed by an IP address cannot hold, password when passwords are forbidden, device_bound_only for a synced passkey, or min_passkeys for a removal it forbids. Absent where no setting is the reason. Left a string rather than an enumeration here, because the policy's own keys are the list and a copy of it would drift.

examples.error: no such thing, or not yours
a namespace may tighten the installation's policy, never loosen it: device_bound_only is true there

base64url.title: Base64url
base64url.description: Bytes written base64url without padding, the Base64URLString Web Authentication's JSON forms use for every binary member, so that what the browser's toJSON() and parseCreationOptionsFromJSON() read and write travels unchanged.

ceremony.title: Ceremony
ceremony.description: Which of the two passkey ceremonies a request belongs to: registration records a new passkey for a user, assertion signs a user in with one they hold. The words are Web Authentication's own.

sessionKind.title: Session kind
sessionKind.description: What a session may do. full reaches every route the principal's grants allow. enrolment is opened by a password where the policy requires a passkey the account does not hold yet, and enrols passkeys and nothing else: it cannot read a workflow, start a run or mint a token. The server records the credential that opened each session, so the difference is known to it rather than kept by convention.

apiTokenValue.title: API token value
apiTokenValue.description: The clear value of an API token, shown once in the answer that mints it and never again, since only its hash is kept. agktoken_ and at least 43 base64url characters, which is 256 bits: the prefix says what the value is before anybody tries it, as agkjoin_ and agkrunner_ do on the wire, so one that leaks into a log can be recognised and revoked by whoever finds it.

enrolmentCode.title: Enrolment code
enrolmentCode.description: A single-use code authorising the enrolment of a passkey for one user and nothing else, good for an hour: the code an enrolment link carries after #, and a recovery code. One kind for both, because both authorise the same thing and are audited as the same action, enrolment.issue. 256 bits, stored hashed, with a prefix so that one found in a chat or a ticket is recognised for what it is.

exchangeCode.title: Exchange code
exchangeCode.description: The one-time code the sign-in page sends the browser back to agk login's loopback address with: single use, good for a minute, and worth nothing without the verifier whose SHA-256 opened the page.

codeChallenge.title: Code challenge
codeChallenge.description: The SHA-256 of agk login's one-time verifier, base64url without padding, as RFC 7636 computes S256: 43 characters. The only method there is, so no method is named: a verifier sent in the clear would be a code anyone on the way could complete.

codeVerifier.title: Code verifier
codeVerifier.description: agk login's one-time verifier, as RFC 7636 writes one: 43 to 128 unreserved characters. It never leaves agk until the exchange, which is what makes a code seen on the way worthless.

loopbackUri.title: Loopback address
loopbackUri.description: Where agk login listens: plain http on a port of the loopback interface, by address and never by the name localhost, as RFC 8252 advises for a native application's redirect, since a name can be resolved elsewhere and an address cannot. Nothing else is accepted, so the sign-in page can never be made to hand a code to another host.

terminalSignIn.title: Terminal sign-in
terminalSignIn.description: What agk login handed the sign-in page, passed on by the page with the sign-in it completes, so that the answer sends the browser back to agk with a one-time code. The two travel together: a loopback address without a challenge would be a code anybody on the machine could redeem.

redirect_uri.description: The loopback address agk login listens on, as the sign-in page was opened with it.

code_challenge.description: The SHA-256 of agk login's verifier, as the sign-in page was opened with it. The exchange holds the verifier to it.

PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON.title: PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON
PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON.description: Web Authentication's PublicKeyCredentialDescriptorJSON: one credential, named so that an authenticator can recognise it. Spelled as the Recommendation spells it, and left open, because it is the browser's dictionary and a member it adds is one this document does not own.

type.description: Always public-key, the one credential type Web Authentication defines.

id.description: The credential ID, as the credentials list names the passkey.

transports.description: How the authenticator holding it was reached when it was registered, as the browser reported: a hint for the browser, never something the API decides with.

PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON.title: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON
PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON() takes to start a registration. Spelled as the Recommendation spells it, camel case included, because the browser reads it and an identifier is never translated; left open, because a member a later browser reads is not this document's to refuse. The members listed are the ones the API sets.

id.description: The Relying Party Identifier, a domain and never an IP address, which a browser refuses.

name.description: What the authenticator shows the person as the site the passkey is for.

rp.description: The Relying Party: the installation, named by the host of AGK_PUBLIC_URL, or of AGK_PROXY_URL behind a proxy, which is the origin the browser checks the page against.

id.description: The user handle, random bytes the API minted for the account, which an assertion hands back as userHandle.

name.description: The login, which the authenticator shows to tell accounts apart.

displayName.description: The display name, shown beside the login.

user.description: The user being enrolled. Its id is a user handle the API minted, never the login, because Web Authentication asks that the handle carry nothing that identifies the person.

challenge.description: A fresh random challenge, single use, which the attestation must sign over.

pubKeyCredParams.description: The key types the API verifies, in order of preference: ES256 (-7), EdDSA (-8) and RS256 (-257), the three COSE algorithms it checks with the Go standard library.

timeout.description: How long, in milliseconds, the ceremony may take before the challenge is abandoned.

excludeCredentials.description: The passkeys the user already holds, so that an authenticator does not register a second one for the same account.

residentKey.description: Always required: the passkey is discoverable, which is what lets an assertion start without naming the user.

requireResidentKey.description: true, the Level 1 spelling of the same request, for authenticators that read only that.

userVerification.description: The policy's user_verification: required makes the passkey two factors, the authenticator and whatever unlocks it.

authenticatorSelection.description: What is asked of the authenticator: a discoverable credential, so that signing in needs no login typed first, and the user verification the policy imposes.

attestation.description: Always none. Attestation would certify the authenticator's make, and the synced passkeys most people hold carry none, so asking for it would refuse them or prove nothing.

PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON.title: PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON
PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.parseRequestOptionsFromJSON() takes to start a sign-in. Spelled as the Recommendation spells it and left open, as its creation counterpart is.

challenge.description: A fresh random challenge, single use, which the assertion must sign.

timeout.description: How long, in milliseconds, the ceremony may take.

rpId.description: The Relying Party Identifier, the host of AGK_PUBLIC_URL or of AGK_PROXY_URL behind a proxy.

allowCredentials.description: Always empty: the authenticator offers whichever passkey it holds for this Relying Party, so no login is sent before the ceremony and none can be probed for.

RegistrationResponseJSON.title: RegistrationResponseJSON
RegistrationResponseJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's RegistrationResponseJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() returns after navigator.credentials.create(). Sent as the browser serialised it: spelled as the Recommendation spells it and left open, the one object in a request body here that is, because refusing a member a newer browser adds would refuse the browser.

rawId.description: The same ID, which Web Authentication carries twice; the API holds the two to each other.

clientDataJSON.description: The client data the browser assembled: the type webauthn.create, the challenge and the origin, which the API holds to the options it issued and to its own origin.

authenticatorData.description: The authenticator data, also inside the attestation object, where the API reads it: the Relying Party's hash, the flags, Backup Eligibility and Backup State among them, and the new credential's key.

transports.description: How the authenticator was reached, kept with the passkey and handed back in excludeCredentials.

publicKey.description: The new public key as SubjectPublicKeyInfo, a convenience the browser adds. Not read: the key recorded is the one in the attestation object.

publicKeyAlgorithm.description: The COSE algorithm of the new key, a convenience the browser adds. Not read, for the same reason.

attestationObject.description: The attestation object in CBOR: the format, none being the one the API asks for, and the authenticator data. Decoded by the API's own CBOR decoder, which refuses indefinite lengths, duplicate map keys and trailing bytes.

response.description: The authenticator's attestation response. The API reads clientDataJSON and attestationObject, and decodes the key from the attestation object itself rather than trusting the conveniences beside it.

authenticatorAttachment.description: platform for an authenticator built into the device, cross-platform for one reached over USB, NFC or a phone. Informative only.

clientExtensionResults.description: The results of any extension the browser ran. The API asks for none, and reads nothing here.

AuthenticationResponseJSON.title: AuthenticationResponseJSON
AuthenticationResponseJSON.description: Web Authentication Level 3's AuthenticationResponseJSON, what PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() returns after navigator.credentials.get(). Sent as the browser serialised it, spelled as the Recommendation spells it and left open, as the registration response is.

id.description: The ID of the passkey that signed, which names the account.

clientDataJSON.description: The client data: the type webauthn.get, the challenge and the origin, held to the options issued and to the API's own origin.

authenticatorData.description: The authenticator data: the Relying Party's hash, the flags, user verification and Backup State among them, and the signature counter.

signature.description: The signature over the authenticator data and the hash of the client data, checked with the key the passkey was registered with.

userHandle.description: The user handle the passkey was registered under, which a discoverable credential hands back so that the account is known without a login typed.

authenticatorAttachment.description: platform or cross-platform, as for a registration. Informative only.

clientExtensionResults.description: The results of any extension the browser ran. Nothing here is read.

passkeyOptionsRequest.title: Passkey options request
passkeyOptionsRequest.description: Which ceremony to start. An assertion names nobody, since the passkey the authenticator offers names the account. A registration is for the caller's own account where a session is presented, or for the account an enrolment code was issued for where one is given instead.

ceremony.description: registration to record a new passkey, assertion to sign in with one.

code.description: The code of an enrolment link or a recovery code, for a registration by someone who has no session: the enrolment page reads it from after the # of its own address, which a browser never sends, and hands it here. It is held against the challenge and consumed by the verification that records the passkey, so a ceremony dismissed halfway does not burn it. Refused beside an assertion.

passkeyOptions.title: Passkey options
passkeyOptions.description: The options of the ceremony started, for the page to hand to the browser as they are.

ceremony.description: The ceremony these options start, as asked.

options.description: Web Authentication's own options: PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptionsJSON for a registration, PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptionsJSON for an assertion.

passkeyVerifyRequest.title: Passkey verification request
passkeyVerifyRequest.description: The browser's answer to the options, and what the page adds to it: a label for a new passkey, and agk login's loopback address and challenge for a sign-in it started.

ceremony.description: The ceremony being finished, the same as the options were asked for.

credential.description: What PublicKeyCredential.toJSON() returned: a RegistrationResponseJSON for a registration, an AuthenticationResponseJSON for an assertion.

label.description: A name for the new passkey, so that two on two devices can be told apart when one is lost. Registration only.

terminal.description: What agk login opened the sign-in page with, where it did. Assertion only: the answer then carries the loopback address to send the browser to.

redirectTo.title: Redirect to agk login
redirectTo.description: Where the sign-in page sends the browser once a sign-in agk login started has succeeded: the loopback address agk login gave, with the one-time code as its code query parameter, which agk then trades at POST /api/v1/auth/exchange. The API writes the whole address rather than the page assembling it, so that the page can never be made to send a code anywhere the API did not check.

passkeyVerified.title: Passkey verified
passkeyVerified.description: What a verified ceremony did. A registration answers the passkey it recorded. An assertion answers who signed in, the session itself being the cookie set beside it, and, for a sign-in agk login started, where to send the browser next.

login.description: The account the ceremony was for: the one that enrolled, or the one that signed in.

credential.description: The passkey recorded, as the credentials list will show it, kind and flags included. Registration only.

redirect_to.description: Where the page sends the browser next. Present only for an assertion that carried terminal.

passwordLoginRequest.title: Password sign-in request
passwordLoginRequest.description: A login and a password, the fallback an installation can forbid, with a TOTP code where the account holds a generator.

password.description: The password, compared with its Argon2id hash and never stored or logged as sent.

totp.description: The current code of the account's TOTP generator, required where the account holds one and refused where it does not. A TOTP exists only alongside a password.

terminal.description: What agk login opened the sign-in page with, where it did: the way agk login signs in on an installation addressed by an IP address, where no passkey can be used.

signIn.title: Signed in
signIn.description: Who signed in with a password and what the session opened may do. The session itself is the cookie set beside this answer.

session.description: full, or enrolment where the policy requires a passkey the account does not hold yet.

redirect_to.description: Where the page sends the browser next, for a sign-in agk login started. Never beside an enrolment-only session, which cannot mint a token.

exchangeRequest.title: Code exchange request
exchangeRequest.description: agk login's code and verifier, the two halves of PKCE, named as RFC 7636 names them.

code.description: The code the browser brought back to the loopback address.

code_verifier.description: The verifier whose SHA-256 opened the sign-in page.

device_label.description: What the token is for, shown when tokens are listed: agk writes the machine's name.

issuedToken.title: Issued token
issuedToken.description: A token just minted: its value, this once, and its record as the list will show it without the value from now on.

token.description: The clear value, for the Authorization header. Shown here and nowhere else, ever: lose it and mint another.

api_token.description: The token's record: its identifier, which revoking it names, its principal, label, scope and expiry.

notification.title: Notification
notification.description: Something the installation tells the caller of its own accord. One kind so far: an administrator widened their own access in a namespace the caller owns, which is how an administrator reads another namespace's payloads, since they hold no run:read_data of their own. Owners do not read the audit log, and the people whose data it is should hear it from the installation itself.

kind.description: What happened. admin_access_widened: an administrator wrote a grant for themselves, and grant says which.

namespace.description: The namespace concerned, one the caller owns.

grant.description: The grant the administrator wrote, principal and granted_by being the same person.

me.title: Me
me.description: Who the caller is and what it may do at this moment: its principal, the record behind it, its groups, its effective permissions, and its notifications. The permissions are what the grants resolve to now, the principal's own and its groups', at both scopes, with every deny subtracted, and narrowed by the presenting token's scope where it has one, so that a client hides what the caller does not hold rather than disabling it.

principal.description: The caller as a grant and the audit log write it: a login, or NS/NAME for a service account; operator for the bootstrap token until the first administrator has enrolled.

admin.description: Whether the caller is a platform administrator: a user created with admin, or the bootstrap token, which is one until the first administrator has enrolled. It grants no run:read_data anywhere.

user.description: The caller's account, where the caller is a user.

service_account.description: The caller's record, where the caller is a service account.

groups.description: The groups the caller belongs to, as a grant names them. Empty for a service account, which belongs to a namespace rather than to a team.

permissions.description: The caller's effective permissions, keyed by scope as a grant writes it. A namespace's key holds what applies to every workflow in it; a workflow's key, NS/NAME, appears where a grant or a deny on that workflow changes that, and holds the whole of what applies there. A scope the caller holds nothing at is absent.

notifications.description: What the installation has to tell the caller, newest first. No route marks one read yet, so the list is what happened.

credentialList.title: Credential list
credentialList.description: The caller's credentials, each described and none held: no public key, no hash, no shared secret.

credentials.description: Passkeys, the password where one is still stored, and a TOTP generator where one is enrolled, oldest first. Empty for a service account, which holds tokens only.

tokenRequest.title: Token request
tokenRequest.description: What to mint. Every member is optional: an empty object mints a token for the caller, expiring in 90 days, with the caller's full rights.

principal.description: Whose token it is: the caller's own login, or a service account of a namespace the caller owns, written NS/NAME. Absent means the caller. Never a group, which holds no credential.

device_label.description: What the token is minted on or for, so that a list of tokens can be read and the one on a lost machine revoked.

expires_at.description: When the token stops being accepted. Absent means 90 days from now; later than a year from now is refused, so that no token is a credential for good and every one is renewed by someone who still means it.

scope.description: What the token is narrowed to: permissions it keeps and the namespaces and workflows it reaches. It can only narrow: the token's rights are its principal's intersected with it.

tokenList.title: Token list
tokenList.description: API tokens as they are listed: never a value.

tokens.description: The caller's tokens and those of the service accounts of namespaces it owns that are still accepted, newest first; an expired or revoked token is gone from the list.

namespaceCreate.title: Namespace creation
namespaceCreate.description: A shared namespace to create: its name, its owner and its quotas. The record answered is the one GET /api/v1/namespaces lists.

name.description: The namespace's name, the first path segment of its routes. Refused where a namespace or a login already holds it.

kind.description: Always shared, and shared where it is left out. A personal namespace is created on its user's first sign-in and never here.

owner.description: Who owns it: a user or a group. The owner is who hears when an administrator widens their own access in it.

quotas.description: What it may consume. Absent sets no bound of its own; PUT /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/quotas changes them later.

namespaceList.title: Namespace list
namespaceList.description: Namespaces as the caller may see them.

namespaces.description: The namespaces the caller holds a grant in, directly or through a group, or every one for an administrator; its personal namespace among them. By name.

userCreate.title: User creation
userCreate.description: A user to create, as agk user create sends it.

login.description: What the user signs in as, and the name of the personal namespace created on their first sign-in. Refused where a namespace or another user holds it.

display_name.description: The name people read in the console and in the sharing panel.

admin.description: true for a platform administrator, as agk user create --admin asks. false where it is left out.

enrolmentLink.title: Enrolment link
enrolmentLink.description: A link that enrols the first passkey of an account: single use, good for an hour, shown once and stored hashed.

link.description: The enrolment page on the Relying Party's origin, with the code after #. A browser never sends what follows #, so the code reaches no access log, a proxy's included.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, an hour after it was issued.

createdUser.title: Created user
createdUser.description: The user created, and the link that enrols their first passkey.

user.description: The account, as GET /api/v1/users lists it.

enrolment.description: The enrolment link, shown this once.

recoveryCode.title: Recovery code
recoveryCode.description: A recovery code for a user who has lost their passkeys, as a code to read out or type and as a link to the enrolment page carrying it. Single use, good for an hour, authorising the enrolment of a new passkey and nothing else, and never sent by mail, which would put the account back behind a mailbox.

code.description: The code, which the enrolment page takes typed.

link.description: The enrolment page with the code after #, for an administrator handing it over as a link.

expires_at.description: When the code stops working, an hour after it was issued.

users.description: Every user, by login, with no credential in any of them.

groupCreate.title: Group creation
groupCreate.description: A group to create, empty or with its first members.

name.description: The group's name, written after group: wherever a principal is expected. Refused where a group already holds it.

members.description: Its first members, by login. Absent creates it empty; members are added one by one after that.

groups.description: Every group, by name, with its members.

serviceAccountCreate.title: Service account creation
serviceAccountCreate.description: A service account to create in a namespace the caller owns, written NS/NAME from then on.

namespace.description: The namespace it belongs to, one the caller owns.

name.description: Its name within the namespace. agentiik is refused: it is the built-in identity's name in every namespace and no other's.

serviceAccountList.title: Service account list
serviceAccountList.description: Service accounts as the caller may see them.

service_accounts.description: The service accounts of the namespaces the caller owns, the built-in NS/agentiik of each among them, by namespace and then by name.

grantCreate.title: Grant creation
grantCreate.description: A grant or a deny to write at the scope the route names: one principal, and exactly one of a role and a denied permission, with an optional expiry. The scope is the route's, never the body's, so a grant cannot be written anywhere its writer does not hold grant:manage.

principal.description: Who it is for, as a principal is written: a login, group:NAME or NS/NAME.

role.description: The role granted, for an allow.

deny.description: The one permission taken away, for a deny, whatever any allow at any scope gives. A permission and never a role: the payloads kept out of reach are run:read_data alone, and no role is that.

expires_at.description: When it ends by itself. Absent means it lasts until revoked.

grantList.title: Grant list
grantList.description: Grants and denies, each with the scope it was written at.

grants.description: The grants and denies that apply, each with its scope, so that a list for a workflow tells what it inherits from its namespace from what is written on it. An expired grant is left out.

ns.name: ns
ns.description: The namespace, by name. One the caller cannot see is answered as one that does not exist, so that no name can be learnt by asking.

workflow.name: name
workflow.description: The workflow, by the name its metadata.name writes. One the caller cannot see is answered as one that does not exist.

grant.name: id
grant.description: The grant's identifier, as the list gives it and as Terraform imports it.

token.name: id
token.description: The token's identifier, as the list gives it. It is not the token and opens nothing.

group.name: group
group.description: The group, by name, without the group: a principal reference writes before it.

serviceAccountNamespace.name: ns
serviceAccountNamespace.description: The namespace the service account belongs to, the half of NS/NAME before the slash. One the caller does not own is answered as one that does not exist.

serviceAccountName.name: name
serviceAccountName.description: The service account's name, the half of NS/NAME after the slash.

credential.name: id
credential.description: The credential to remove, by the id the list gives it: a passkey's credential ID, or the identifier the engine minted for a password or a TOTP generator. A query parameter because the route names the collection and no path segment below it.

redirectUri.name: redirect_uri
redirectUri.description: The loopback address agk login listens on, where it opened the page. Given with code_challenge or not at all.

codeChallenge.name: code_challenge
codeChallenge.description: The SHA-256 of agk login's verifier, where it opened the page. Given with redirect_uri or not at all.

setSession.description: The session cookie, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax, set for the whole origin. Its value is opaque and means nothing outside the server that keeps it.

noStore.description: no-store, on every answer carrying a secret shown once, so that no cache on the way keeps a copy of it.

wwwAuthenticate.description: Bearer, the scheme the route authenticates with besides the session cookie.

badRequest.description: The body is refused before it is read as a request: not JSON, not UTF-8, a field the route does not read, a field written twice, anything after the document, or a value outside its grammar.

unknown field.summary: a field the route does not read

value.error: the body holds a field this route does not read: kind

unauthorised.description: No credential, or one that is not accepted: expired, revoked, unknown, or the session of an account suspended since.

forbidden.description: The caller is known and may not do this.

not held.summary: a permission or a role not held

value.error: you do not hold what this needs
this session enrols passkeys and nothing else

notFound.description: Nothing there, or nothing the caller may see: the same answer for both, so that asking teaches nothing.

value.error: no such thing, or not yours

conflict.description: The request would leave a state the rules forbid.

value.error: removing this passkey would leave fewer than min_passkeys

tooLarge.description: A body past 64 KiB, the cap the API's other small bodies carry.

value.error: the body is larger than 64 KiB

unprocessable.description: The body is well formed and names something that is not there or not the caller's, or an instant outside what the route allows. One sentence for the absent and the hidden alike.

absent.summary: a principal that does not exist

value.error: expires_at is more than a year away
